newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Budget chair says Russian budget won't pass in '96.
newsitem.headline: Budget chair says Russian budget won't pass in '96.

text.p: Russia will not pass its 1997 budget by the end of this year, Mikhail Zadornov, chairman of the State Duma lower house of parliament's budget committee, said on Tuesday.
He told reporters the administration was unwilling to present to the Duma the version of the budget which had been agreed in the trilateral reconciliation commission working on an acceptable draft.
No comment from the finance ministry was immediately available.

The Duma rejected the government's first draft of the budget last month. Since then a reconciliation commission, in which both houses of parliament and the government are represented, has been working on a new version.
The reconciliation commission is due to have a final meeting on Wednesday, with the Duma giving the budget a new first reading on November 20.
"We can already say that the budget as a whole, without doubt, will not pass the Duma by the end of the year," he said.
There is no legal framework to cover failure to pass the budget, but parliament has faced the problem every year of Russia's independence except 1996 and has in the past approved temporary budgets.
Zadornov said parts of the budget would be passed eventually but because neither parliament nor the government would take responsibility for the budget it might not happen this month.
"The work of the commission is being drawn out because no one wants to take responsibility for making a decision on the budget -- neither the majority of parliament nor the government."
Russia is trying to keep to a small deficit in 1997 under pressure from the International Monetary Fund, but the Duma is eager to increase budget spending to a starved economy.

"The government is taking a break for negotiations with parliamentary groups -- primarily negotiations with the largest groups," he said. Communists and their allies are the largest group in the Duma.
Zadornov said the government was also afraid the Duma could reject the budget a second time.
This would build up pressure for a no-confidence vote.
